I’ve sat in on enough vendor calls in Noida’s IT corridor to notice a pattern. It’s not bad code. It’s not bad pricing. It’s a single word that means two different things depending on who’s saying it: “website.”
Here’s how it usually goes.
A business owner tells a “web design company” they need a new website. The designer nods, delivers a beautiful Figma file three weeks later, and hands over the invoice. The owner is thrilled — until they ask, “So when does it go live?” and the answer is some version of: “Oh, you’ll need a developer for that part.”
Nobody lied. The designer designed. That’s what “design” means. But the business owner heard “website” and assumed the whole thing — layout, CMS, hosting, the contact form that actually emails them — was covered.
Case One: The ₹35,000 Surprise
A boutique in Sector 18 paid a design studio ₹18,000 for a homepage mockup. Gorgeous work. Then they needed someone to actually build it in WordPress, wire up the product catalog, and connect a payment gateway. That was another ₹35,000 to a completely different vendor — who had to reverse-engineer the designer’s intent from static PNG files instead of working live with the design team.
Case Two: The CMS Nobody Could Use
A clinic in Indirapuram hired a “full-service” agency that, it turned out, meant “we design, and our cousin’s company builds it.” The handoff was rough. The final CMS had fields the clinic’s front-desk staff couldn’t figure out, because the people who built the admin panel had never spoken to the people who’d actually use it day to day.
Case Three: The One That Worked
A logistics startup near Sector 62 asked one question before signing anything: “Will the same team that designs this also build the CMS?” The agency said yes, and could show three past projects proving it. No handoff gap. No “that wasn’t in scope.” The site shipped on time because one team owned the whole outcome.
The Actual Difference
Web design = how it looks and how people move through it. Web development = the code, the CMS, and anything that needs to function — payment gateways, CRM sync, custom dashboards.
Some Noida agencies are genuinely strong at both. Many are strong at one and quietly outsource the other. Neither is a scandal — it’s just something you need to know before you sign, not after.
If you want the fuller breakdown — including what CMS-only builds should cost versus custom development, and the exact questions to ask before hiring either type of vendor — aNquest Media put together a plain-language comparison that would have saved all three businesses above a fair amount of money and back-and-forth.
The lesson isn’t “hire a full-service agency.” It’s: ask which half of the job you’re actually paying for, before the invoice tells you the hard way.
